title: Voice script
description: The narration of one variant: every line with the second it comes in on, how long it is expected to run, and whether the music ducks under it. It is written as voice-script.json next to the variant's MP4. This file is the contract; the plain-text voice-script.txt that ships to the user is generated FROM it, never the other way round.

lang.description: BCP-47 tag of the run's output language. The lines are written in it AND the voice has to speak it: a script in one language read by a voice from another is the first thing anybody notices.

video.description: The rendered MP4 these seconds refer to. The seconds come from that spec's grid, not from your ear.

video_duration_s.description: No line may start after this.

voice.description: The voice that was used or is meant to be used. Synthetic and freely licensed; never a clone of a real person.

engine.description: 'none' means the variant ships without voice and this file is what lets the user add it.

duck_db.description: How far the music and the clip audio drop while a line with duck=true is speaking. This is the field that stops anybody lowering a clip's audio by hand: the builder applies it at render time.

duck_pad_s.description: Seconds of ramp before and after the line, so the duck does not click.

notes.description: For whoever edits the file. Never synthesized.

text.description: Exactly as it will be heard, in the output language. No quotes, no stage directions, no character names. Short, 6 to 14 words. Numbers written as words: 'twenty minutes', not '20 min'. Pauses come from commas and periods, never from stretching the audio.

start_s.description: The second the speaking starts. Taken from the spec's grid (beats x 60/bpm, or dur), inside the segment the line refers to.

duration_hint_s.description: How long you expect the line to run, so the next one can be placed before it is synthesized. Once the WAVs exist, check the real durations: t[i] + duration[i] < t[i+1], or two voices talk at once.

duck.description: Duck the music and the clip audio under this line by duck_db. false only when the line is meant to fight the sound on purpose.

emphasis.description: Delivery of this line. 'strong' is for the hook and the payoff; using it on every line flattens all of them.

wav.description: The generated file for this line, l0.wav, l1.wav... in index order, alongside durations.json. That pair is the contract any voice source has to leave.
